old_title: Ukraine latest: Two dead and oil refinery in flames after drone attack on Moscow
new_title: Ukraine war live: Trump urges Zelensky to stop hitting Putin's refineries
old_text:
Two people were killed after Ukrainian forces fired more than 1,000 drones at Russia overnight.
Moscow's mayor described the wave of drones as the "largest ever" attack on the Russian capital, setting alight an oil refinery and a residential building.
Across the wider Moscow region, the attack killed two people and wounded 20, local Governor Andrei Vorobyov said. The dead were a 74-year-old man and a 44-year-old woman, he said.
A video posted on social media by Volodoymr Zelensky showed footage of flames tearing across buildings and large plumes of black smoke rising from the blazing oil refinery.
The Ukrainian president said: "Our long-range responses had a very significant impact in the Moscow region last night. One of Russia's key oil industry facilities and the aggressor's logistics facility were hit."
The attack came as the Kremlin was wrapping up the third and last day of its parliamentary elections.
Ukraine denounced the election as illegal because it included residents of regions Moscow has illegally annexed from Ukraine to tighten president Vladimir Putin's 26-year grip on power.
Most anti-war candidates were barred from the ballot.
Editorial: Russia has changed the nature of its warfare - so must we
The rise in unlawful drone activity at MoD sites - as revealed by The Independent - is the latest sign we are engaged in a new form of conflict with Russia. If Britain is to win this 'warm war', we must bolster our defences, not simply to protect ourselves, but to deter further aggression.
Read our editorial here:
Russian drone strike on monastery in Kherson region kills member of clergy- Zelensky
A Russian drone struck a men's monastery in the Kherson region, killing a clergy member and injuring four others, Volodymyr Zekensky has said.
In a post on X, the Ukrainian president wrote: "Yesterday, in the Kherson region, the Russians struck a monastery with an FPV drone. Tragically, one member of the monastery clergy was killed and four others were wounded. My condolences to the family and loved ones."
The president added: "There were strikes on critical and civilian infrastructure in the Kharkiv, Sumy, and Odesa regions. In the Dnipro and Zaporizhzhia regions, residential buildings were hit. Since the evening, the Vinnytsia, Kyiv, Zhytomyr, and Cherkasy regions have also come under attack."
Slovakia's leader warns Europe is closer than ever to a large-scale war
Slovakia's leader has warned Europe is closer than ever to large-scale war erupting.
In a video posted on X, Robert Fico said Europe faces a "mortal danger" while watching the West "pour fuel on the fire" with its support for Ukraine.
He added: "The failure of the strategy to destroy Russia through the war in Ukraine has led some Western politicians to believe that if the goal cannot be achieved through the Ukrainian army and full support for it, then every effort must be made to trigger a conflict between NATO and Russia."
Watch: Kyiv downs jet-powered Shaheds with new interceptor drones
Moscow mayor accuses Ukraine of attempting to disrupt Russian elections with overnight attack
Moscow Mayor Sergei Sobyanin said that 450 drones had been destroyed en route to the Russian capital, and that the attack had damaged the Moscow Oil Refinery and a residential building.
He said the "unprecedented attack" on Moscow was an attempt to disrupt the elections. "The enemy failed in this regard," he said.
Ukraine's military struck an oil refinery in Moscow region, Zelensky says
Ukraine's military struck an oil refinery in Russia's Moscow region overnight, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky said on Sunday.
"One of Russia's key oil industry facilities and the aggressor's logistics facility were hit. These are billions of dollars that sustain the war machine," Zelensky said on X.
Russian drone attack killed a mother and her two small children in Kyiv region
A Russian drone attack killed a mother and her two 3-year-old children in Ukraine's Kyiv region overnight, the emergency service said on Sunday.
The drone strike hit a private home, the service said.
Russia has been attacking the capital Kyiv and the surrounding Kyiv region with drones continually in recent weeks.
Slovak PM Fico says some in West seek war between Russia and Nato
Some Western politicians are seeking conflict between Nato and Russia after a "failed" strategy to defeat Moscow in its war with Ukraine, Slovak prime minister Robert Fico said on Saturday.
Longtime Slovak leader Fico, who has kept up warm relations with Russia and refuses military aid for Ukraine, said this week that Europe was closer than ever to a large-scale war erupting from the Ukraine war.
At the same time, some European leaders, such as those in France and Poland, have warned of Russian hybrid attacks.
In his video message, Fico said, "We face a mortal danger" while watching the West "pour fuel on the fire" with its support for Ukraine, which he said had been to no avail.
"The failure of the strategy to destroy Russia through the war in Ukraine has led some Western politicians to believe that if the goal cannot be achieved through the Ukrainian army and full support for it, then every effort must be made to trigger a conflict between Nato and Russia," Fico said in the video posted on social media.
He said the war in Ukraine was not Slovakia's nor Nato's war but said, "Certain war hawks within Nato are trying, at any cost, to turn this war into a conflict between Russia and Nato."
Earlier this week, Fico warned a drone incursion could spark the activation of Nato's collective defence clause and he wanted to prevent Slovakia - which neighbours Ukraine and is a member of the Nato military alliance - from becoming part of an armed conflict.
He said on Saturday that creating a pretext to start a war was easy and reiterated Slovakia would not send soldiers to fight under a fabricated pretext.
Ukraine denounces Russia's inclusion of annexed regions in parliamentary elections
Ukraine has denounced Moscow for including residents of regions it illegally annexed from Ukraine in Russia's parliamentary elections for the first time since the start of the war.
Kyiv officials called the voting illegal, while a human rights activist said residents in the territories were being coerced into participating in the poll, which forms part of Kremlin efforts to consolidate its gains in Ukraine.
Voting across Russia began on Friday and runs until Sunday. However, balloting in the annexed Ukrainian territories and some areas on the Russian side of the border has been under way since the end of last month, with Russian officials citing security concerns for the extended voting period.
Russian authorities say the Donetsk, Luhansk, Kherson and Zaporizhzhia regions - annexed by Russia in September 2022 in a move not recognised internationally - have more than 3.5 million eligible voters.
Kyiv authorities have called the voting in those territories illegal and urged foreign governments and international organisations not to recognise the election.
They also warned Ukrainians that taking part in organising the vote for the State Duma, Russia's lower house of parliament, could carry criminal liability.
Russian president Vladimir Putin has emphasised the importance of voting in the territories in an election intended to demonstrate public support for the war. The ruling pro-Putin United Russia party is widely expected to retain its dominance.
Two killed in Moscow region after attack with hundreds of drones, mayor says
Hundreds of drones targeted Moscow and the surrounding region on Sunday, killing at least two people and damaging a major oil refinery as Russia's three-day parliamentary election drew to a close, authorities claimed.
Moscow mayor Sergei Sobyanin said more than 1,600 drones had been intercepted and shot down, including 450 targeting the capital.
Sobyanin accused Ukraine of attempting to disrupt the tightly controlled election, saying the "unprecedented attack" had been planned to interfere with the vote.
"The enemy did not succeed," he said on Telegram.
Moscow region governor Andrey Vorobyov said two people - a 44-year-old woman and an elderly man - were killed at separate locations.
A drone crash also caused a fire at a 21-storey building, prompting the evacuation of about 400 people, Vorobyov said.
A facility at the Moscow oil refinery was damaged, according to Sobyanin. No casualties were reported there.
Ukraine has not commented on the attacks.
new_text:
Donald Trump has warned Volodymyr Zelensky to halt Ukraine's long-range strike on oil refineries across Russia ahead of a meeting in New York this week, it has been reported.
"Diesel, diesel... diesel," was the US President's main message to his Ukrainian counterpart during a phone call that came hours before Vladimir Putin's United Russia claimed a record number of seats in the parliamentary election, further cementing his grip on power.
A senior White House official familiar with the conversation between the two leaders said Trump was worried that the Ukrainian attacks are exacerbating a global diesel shortage and pushing up prices, the FT reported.
After the call, Zelensky said he will meet Trump on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly. He further warned that Russia is "sending many signals" that it is ready to expand the war.
This comes as Vladimir Putin's United Russia has claimed a record number of seats hours after polls closed in the first parliamentary election since the start of the full-scale invasion, further cementing his grip on power.
Results from over 95% of the polling stations gave the governing party just under 58% of the vote for the 225 seats apportioned by parties, according to the Central Election Commission.
Arrests, armed soldiers and opposition parties banned: How Putin controlled Russia's 'sham' elections
Vladimir Putin's party is set to win by a comfortable majority as voting closed in the country's tightly-controlled parliamentary elections, widely branded a sham.
Initial data from Russia's Central Election Commission suggests the leader's United Russia party is in the lead to win with 57.8 per cent of the votes and over 90 per cent of the ballots processed.
Kaja Kallas proposes EU sanctions over 'sham' elections in occupied Ukraine
Kaja Kallas has announced plans to propose sanctions on those who facilitated the State Duma elections in occupied Ukrainian territories.
Reiterating that European Union does not recognise the "sham" results, the Vice-President of the European Commission said: "Those involved in organising these sham elections or standing as candidates in the temporarily occupied territories of Ukraine, as well as those responsible for undermining the possibility of free and fair elections inside Russia, will be sanctioned."
Putin should have suffered in Russia's latest election. He has Trump to thank for his success
Russians went to the polls for elections to its parliament amid a fuel crisis, mortuaries swollen with war dead, and an economy that is shrinking.
All ingredients pointed to what should have been a landslide against the ruling United Russia Party.
But with more than 90 per cent of the results counted, Vladimir Putin's rubber-stamp-representatives are sitting more than comfortably, with 58 per cent of the votes.
Trump warns Zelensky to 'halt strikes on Russia's oil refineries over diesel prices'
Donald Trump has warned Volodymyr Zelensky to halt Ukraine's long-range strike on oil refineries across Russia ahead of their meeting in New York later this week, it has been reported.
"Diesel, diesel... diesel," was the US President's main message to his Ukrainian counterpart during a phone call on Sunday.
A senior White House official familiar with the conversation between the two leaders said Trump was worried that the Ukrainian attacks are exacerbating a global diesel shortage and pushing up prices, the FT reported.
This is the second time in less than a week that Trump has called on Zelensky "to stop knocking out diesel fuel in Russia."
The US President himself is feeling the pressure at home as the US war on Iran has curtailed oil shipments through the Strait of Hormuz.
"We spoke to Mr.Zelensky about it," Trump told reporters.
"There are plenty of other targets. Don't hit diesel fuel, because that's hurting, that's hurting the world."
Chechen warlord Kadyrov wins election 'nearly 100% of vote'
Chechen warlord Ramzan Kadyrov has been re-elected to a fifth term, with almost 100 percent of the vote.
A close ally to Vladimir Putin, Kadyrov has been allowed to run the southern, mainly Muslim region of Chechnya, as a criminal state.
Human rights organisations have long accused his brutal regime of torture, enforced disappearances, and extrajudicial killings.
Russia's Central Electoral Commission said Kadyrov took 99.85 percent of the vote in Chechnya, slightly up from 99.73 percent in 2021.
International observers have in the past sharply criticised the conduct of elections in the small mountainous region.
Kadyrov, who rejects such criticism as Western-backed attempts to undermine his rule, regularly stresses his personal loyalty to Putin and has championed a hard line on Ukraine, where he says his Chechen forces have been fighting since 2022.
Britain condemns Russian elections in occupied Ukrainian territories as 'illegal'
Britain has condemned Russia's "sham" elections in occupied Ukrainian territories in a joint statement with Australia, Canada, New Zealand and Norway.
"These sham elections are part of a wider system of occupation: the imposition of Russian administration, law, media, education, language and citizenship, backed by coercion and repression.," it said.
"This includes reports of the enforced disappearance, detention, and torture of thousands of Ukrainian citizens."
Voting was held for the second time in the annexed Crimean Pensisula and for the first in Donetsk, Kherson, Luhansk and Zaporizhzhia.
"These regions are part of Ukraine and holding sham elections cannot alter the status of these territories under international law," the statement added.
How other parties did in 'sham' Russian election
Communist Party of the Russian Federation - 13.8 percent
Liberal Democratic Party of Russia - 8.9 percent
New People party - 7.9 percent
Ella Pamfilova, chair of Russia's Central Election Commission, said the Fair Russia party was said to have a "good chance" of clearing 5 percent of the vote.
She also called the vote "clean" in the face of allegations from opposition activists in exile of widespread rigging.
Voter turnout was recorded at 59.3%, the Tass state news agency reported.
Russia could be 'stockpiling' ballistic missiles for winter
Russia has significantly reduced the deployment of ballistic missiles in attacks on Ukraine, suggesting it may be stockpiling them for winter, it has been reported.
Ballistic missiles inflict some of the heaviest damage, and can only be countered with ABM systems, like the US Patriots, which is running low on.
'No progress' in negotiations, Putin spokesperson says
Dmitry Peskov, spokesperson for Vladimir Putin, has confirmed there has been "no progress so far in the negotiation process regarding Ukraine".
His statement to the Tass state news agency comes as Volodymyr Zelensky said he will travel to New York to meet with Donald Trump on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly.
Reports of Ukrainian 'frustration' with Steve Witkoff are 'false'
Volodymyr Zelensky'c chief negotiator has praised the work of US envoy Steve Witkoff after reports that the Ukrainian government was "growing increasingly frustrated" with him, it was reported.
Rustem Umerov, who is also the head of Ukraine's Foreign Intelligence Service, insisted that a Kyiv Independent story the frustration with Witkoff is "false.
"I believe that the work of American negotiators should be assessed by people who are directly involved in the negotiation process and work closely with Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner," he told Axios.
